# Artificial Intelligence Systems Management Standard

## 1. Purpose

This Standard establishes requirements for the governance, risk management, operational oversight, and lifecycle management of artificial intelligence (AI) systems deployed or under development at Acme Health. This Standard applies the NIST AI Risk Management Framework to ensure AI systems achieve their intended purposes while managing risks to patients, staff, and organizational operations.

## 2. Scope

This Standard applies to all AI systems developed, procured, deployed, or operated by Acme Health, including AI components embedded in clinical, administrative, or operational systems. This Standard applies to all personnel involved in the specification, development, deployment, operation, monitoring, or decommissioning of AI systems.

## 3. AI System Development and Deployment Approval

### 3.1 Go/No-Go Determination

Before an AI system proceeds to production deployment or to the next stage of development, a determination must be made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed. [NIST AI RMF Manage 1.1]

This determination must be documented and retained as part of the AI system's governance record.

## 4. AI Risk Management

### 4.1 Risk Prioritization

Treatment of documented AI risks must be prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods. [NIST AI RMF Manage 1.2]

The prioritization methodology must be documented and applied consistently across all AI systems within scope of this Standard.

### 4.2 Risk Response Planning

Responses to high-priority AI risks must be developed, planned, and documented, with risk response options including mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting. [NIST AI RMF Manage 1.3]

Each documented response plan must identify:

- The specific risk being addressed
- The selected response option (mitigate, transfer, avoid, or accept)
- Actions to be taken
- Responsible parties
- Success criteria

### 4.3 Residual Risk Documentation

Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users must be documented. [NIST AI RMF Manage 1.4]

This documentation must be made available to relevant AI actors, including downstream acquirers and representatives of affected end-user communities.

### 4.4 Risk Treatment Documentation and Monitoring

Risk treatments, response and recovery plans, and communication plans for identified and measured AI risks must be documented and monitored regularly. [NIST AI RMF Manage 4]

## 5. Resource Planning and Alternatives Assessment

Resources required to manage AI risks must be taken into account, along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods, to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts. [NIST AI RMF Manage 2.1]

The alternatives assessment must be documented and included in the planning materials for any proposed AI system deployment or major modification.

## 6. Operational Management of Deployed AI Systems

### 6.1 Value Sustainment

Mechanisms must be in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems. [NIST AI RMF Manage 2.2]

These mechanisms must address ongoing verification that the AI system continues to meet its intended purposes and业objectives as operational conditions and data distributions change over time.

### 6.2 Performance Monitoring and Deactivation

Mechanisms must be in place and applied, and responsibilities must be assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use. [NIST AI RMF Manage 2.4]

The deactivation procedures must include:

- Criteria for determining when performance or outcomes are inconsistent with intended use
- Authority and decision-making process for deactivation
- Communication requirements to affected users and stakeholders
- Procedures for transitioning to alternative processes or systems
- Documentation requirements

### 6.3 Response to Previously Unknown Risks

Procedures must be followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified. [NIST AI RMF Manage 2.3]

These procedures must be documented and accessible to personnel responsible for AI system operations.

## 7. Post-Deployment Monitoring

### 7.1 Monitoring Plan Implementation

Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans must be implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management. [NIST AI RMF Manage 4.1]

Each deployed AI system must have a documented monitoring plan that addresses all elements listed above.

### 7.2 Input Capture and Evaluation

The monitoring plan must establish mechanisms for:

- Capturing input from system users
- Capturing input from other relevant AI actors
- Evaluating captured input for potential risks, performance issues, or improvement opportunities

## 8. Incident and Error Management

### 8.1 Communication of Incidents and Errors

Incidents and errors must be communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. [NIST AI RMF Manage 4.3]

Communication must occur through [Communication Channel] and must include sufficient detail for affected parties to understand the nature and potential impact of the incident or error.

### 8.2 Incident Tracking and Response

Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors must be followed and documented. [NIST AI RMF Manage 4.3]

All incidents and errors related to AI systems must be recorded in [Incident Tracking System]. The record must include:

- Description of the incident or error
- Date and time of occurrence
- Affected AI system(s)
- Impact to users or operations
- Response actions taken
- Recovery actions taken
- Responsible personnel
- Resolution status

## 9. Continual Improvement

### 9.1 Improvement Activities Integration

Measurable activities for continual improvements must be integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors. [NIST AI RMF Manage 4.2]

These activities must be planned and tracked as part of the AI system's lifecycle management process. Engagement with interested parties must occur at [Review Frequency] and must be documented.

## 10. Roles and Responsibilities

Responsibilities for the activities described in this Standard must be assigned and documented. At minimum, the following roles must be explicitly assigned for each AI system:

- AI System Owner: accountable for the AI system's performance and compliance with this Standard
- Risk Manager: responsible for risk assessment, prioritization, and treatment planning
- Operations Manager: responsible for day-to-day monitoring and incident response
- Deactivation Authority: authorized to supersede, disengage, or deactivate the AI system

## 11. Records and Documentation

All documentation required by this Standard must be retained for [Retention Period] and must be accessible to personnel responsible for AI system governance, compliance audits, and post-incident analysis.
